questions.stem: A passenger on a train travelling due north at 160 km/h sees a light due east at 9pm; at 9:45pm the light bears 150°T.

parts.stem: How far did the passenger travel between 9pm and 9:45pm?
parts.hint: 45 minutes is \(\dfrac{45}{60}\) of an hour. Use \(\text{distance}=\text{speed}\times\text{time}\).

steps.explain: 45 minutes is \(\dfrac{45}{60}=\dfrac34\) of an hour. Use \(d=v\times t\).
Evaluate.

parts.stem: How far away is the light from the passenger at 9:45pm? Give your answer as an exact value.
parts.hint: In the triangle formed by the two passenger positions and the light, the angle at the 9pm position is \(90°\) (light due east) and the angle at the 9:45pm position is \(180°-150°=30°\) (measuring from due south). Use the sine rule.

steps.explain: At the 9pm position, the angle between north (toward the 9:45pm position) and east (toward the light) is \(90°\). At the 9:45pm position, the bearing to the light is \(150°\text{T}\), so the angle between south (back toward the 9pm position) and the light is \(180°-150°=30°\).
steps.work: Angle at 9pm position \(=90°\), angle at 9:45pm position \(=30°\)

steps.explain: The third angle (at the light) is \(180°-90°-30°=60°\). Apply the sine rule, using the known side (\(120\text{ km}\)) opposite this \(60°\) angle.
Solve for the distance to the light.
Rationalise the denominator to give the exact value.

questions.stem: A professor is due to be picked up at university by her husband immediately after her last lecture of the day is scheduled to finish. She unexpectedly finishes 3 hours early and immediately begins to walk home at a constant speed of \(6\text{ km/h}\). Her husband, who knows nothing of her early finish, leaves home in his car at exactly the right time in order to meet her at the university at the originally anticipated completion time of her last lecture. On the way to the university he sees his wife and picks her up \(9\text{ km}\) from home. They immediately drive home together and reach home \(2\) hours earlier than was scheduled. Calculate the average speed of the car for its entire journey.
questions.hint: Let \(D\) be the distance from home to university and \(v\) the (constant) car speed. Set up equations for when the husband and wife meet, and for the "2 hours earlier" arrival condition, then solve simultaneously.

steps.explain: Let \(D\) = distance from home to university, \(v\) = constant car speed. Originally, the husband would arrive at university at the lecture's scheduled end time \(t_0\) (leaving home at \(t_0-D/v\)); originally, they would arrive home at \(t_0+D/v\).

She finishes at \(t_0-3\) and walks home; they meet \(9\text{ km}\) from home, so she has walked \(D-9\text{ km}\) by the meeting time. The husband reaches the same meeting point (\(9\text{ km}\) from home) at time \(t_0-\dfrac{D-9}{v}\). Actual arrival home is \(2\) hours earlier than the original \(t_0+D/v\); working through the timing (meeting-time equality and the "2 hours earlier" condition) gives two equations in \(D\) and \(v\).

The meeting-time equation (husband's arrival time at the meeting point = wife's arrival time there) simplifies to a relationship between \(v\) and \((D-9)\); substituting \(D-9=v\) (from the previous step) gives an equation in \(v\) alone.
Solve for \(v\).
Since the car travels at this constant speed \(v\) throughout, the average speed for the whole journey is simply \(v\).

questions.stem: Express the following ratio in the simplest form: \(3\dfrac{1}{4}:\dfrac{2}{5}\)
questions.hint: Turn the mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply both parts by the common denominator (20) to remove the fractions.

steps.explain: Convert \(3\dfrac{1}{4}\) to an improper fraction: \(3\times 4+1=13\), so \(\dfrac{13}{4}\).
Write the ratio with both parts as fractions.
The denominators are 4 and 5: multiply BOTH sides of the ratio by their lowest common multiple, 20.
The ratio is \(65:8\). It cannot be simplified further (65 and 8 have no common factor).
Option B forgot to multiply the second part by 20 properly; the check \(\dfrac{65}{8}=8.125\) equals \(\dfrac{13}{4}\div\dfrac{2}{5}=\dfrac{13}{4}\times\dfrac{5}{2}=\dfrac{65}{8}\) ✓.
So the correct choice is option A.

keyPoints.note: Make both parts whole numbers by multiplying by the common denominator.

questions.hint: Scale \(1:50\) means 1 cm on the drawing is 50 cm in real life. Multiply the drawing length by 50, then convert to metres (\(100\ \text{cm}=1\ \text{m}\)).

steps.explain: Set up equal ratios: drawing : actual \(=1:50\) so \(10:x\) has the same ratio.
The drawing length is multiplied by 50 to get the real length.
Convert to metres: divide by 100.
Option B (500 m) forgets to convert from cm; option D (50 m) is a factor-of-10 slip.
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: A bag contains \(12\) white, \(15\) blue and \(9\) yellow marbles. What is the ratio of blue to yellow marbles?
questions.hint: Write blue FIRST and yellow SECOND (\(15 : 9\)), then divide both numbers by their HCF (\(3\))!

steps.explain: Write the ratio in the exact order requested (blue : yellow): \(15 : 9\).
Find the highest common factor of \(15\) and \(9\): \(\text{HCF}(15, 9) = 3\).
Divide both sides by \(3\): \(15 \div 3 = 5\) and \(9 \div 3 = 3\).
Therefore, the ratio of blue to yellow marbles is \(5 : 3\).

questions.stem: If typing \(875\) words in \(25\) minutes, what typing speed in \(\text{words/min}\) is this?
questions.hint: Divide total words by total minutes: \(875 \div 25\) (remember every \(100\) contains four \(25\)s)!

steps.explain: Use the rate formula: \(\text{Speed} = \dfrac{\text{Words}}{\text{Minutes}}\).
Check: \(35 \times 25 = 875\). Exact!
Therefore, the typing speed is \(35\text{ words/min}\).

questions.stem: Simplify the ratio \(9\text{ cm}\) to \(24\text{ mm}\).
questions.hint: Convert BOTH lengths to the same unit first! \(9\text{ cm} = 90\text{ mm}\), so simplify \(90 : 24\)!

steps.explain: Convert \(9\text{ cm}\) to millimetres using \(1\text{ cm} = 10\text{ mm}\): \(9 \times 10 = 90\text{ mm}\).
Drop the matching units and find \(\text{HCF}(90, 24) = 6\).
Divide both sides by \(6\): \(90 \div 6 = 15\) and \(24 \div 6 = 4\).
Therefore, the simplified ratio is \(15 : 4\).

questions.hint: Add the ratio parts (\(6 + 5 = 11\)), divide \(\$495 \div 11 = \$45\) per part, then multiply \(6 \times \$45\) and \(5 \times \$45\)!

steps.explain: Find the total number of parts: \(6 + 5 = 11\text{ parts}\).
Divide \(\$495\) by \(11\) to find the value of \(1\) part: \(495 \div 11 = 45\).
Calculate each share: \(6 \times \$45 = \$270\) and \(5 \times \$45 = \$225\).

questions.stem: Convert a speed of \(35\text{ m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\).
questions.hint: To convert \(\text{m/s}\) to \(\text{km/h}\), multiply by \(3600\) (seconds in an hour) and divide by \(1000\) (metres in a km) — i.e., multiply by \(3.6\)!

steps.explain: Multiply by \(3600\) to find metres travelled in \(1\text{ hour}\): \(35 \times 3600 = 126{,}000\text{ m/h}\).
Divide by \(1000\) to convert metres to kilometres: \(126{,}000 \div 1000 = 126\text{ km/h}\).
Shortcut check: \(35 \times 3.6 = 126\text{ km/h}\).
Therefore, \(35\text{ m/s} = 126\text{ km/h}\).

questions.stem: Travelling at a speed of \(35\text{ m/s}\) (\(126\text{ km/h}\)), find the distance travelled in \(3\text{ hours}\).
questions.hint: Use \(\text{Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}\) with speed in \(\text{km/h}\) (\(126\text{ km/h}\)) and time in hours (\(3\text{ h}\))!

steps.explain: Use the speed in \(\text{km/h}\) to match the time in hours: \(35\text{ m/s} = 35 \times 3.6 = 126\text{ km/h}\).
Apply \(\text{Distance} = \text{Speed} \times \text{Time}\).
Multiply: \(100 \times 3 + 20 \times 3 + 6 \times 3 = 300 + 60 + 18 = 378\text{ km}\).
Therefore, the distance travelled in \(3\text{ hours}\) is \(378\text{ km}\).
